questions.explanation: Monocots such as maize, rice and guinea grass have parallel-veined leaves, one cotyledon, fibrous roots and scattered vascular bundles. The other options are features of dicots.

whyNot.D: Maize has a fibrous root system; a tap root is typical of dicots such as beans.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Root hair cells take up mineral ions from the soil even when the ions are more concentrated inside the cell than in the soil. This uptake is by
questions.explanation: Moving ions against a concentration gradient needs energy from respiration (ATP) and carrier proteins in the cell membrane. This is active transport.

whyNot.A: Diffusion only moves substances from a higher to a lower concentration.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. It is the only vein in the adult body that carries oxygenated blood.

whyNot.A: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
whyNot.B: The aorta carries oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which bacterium lives in the root nodules of leguminous plants such as groundnut and cowpea and fixes atmospheric nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Rhizobium in legume root nodules changes nitrogen gas from the air into nitrogen compounds the plant can use. This is why farmers plant legumes to enrich the soil.

whyNot.C: Nitrosomonas is a nitrifying bacterium that changes ammonium compounds to nitrites in the soil.
whyNot.D: Pseudomonas includes denitrifying bacteria, which return nitrogen to the air.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Red-green colour blindness is a sex-linked recessive trait. A woman who is a carrier marries a man with normal vision. What is the probability that any son they have will be colour blind?
questions.explanation: A son gets his Y chromosome from his father and one X from his mother. The carrier mother (XᴺXⁿ) passes on Xⁿ half the time, so half of the sons are expected to be colour blind.

whyNot.A: 1/4 is the fraction of ALL children (sons and daughters) expected to be colour-blind sons, not the fraction of sons.
whyNot.D: 0 would be the answer for daughters, who all get a normal X from their father.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which organism has both plant-like and animal-like features, since it has chloroplasts but also moves with a flagellum and has no cell wall?
questions.explanation: Euglena photosynthesises with its chloroplasts like a plant, but swims with a flagellum, has an eyespot and lacks a cellulose cell wall like an animal.

whyNot.A: Spirogyra has chloroplasts but also a cellulose cell wall and cannot move about, so it is plant-like only.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which structure is found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall outside the cell membrane, which gives them a fixed shape. Animal cells have only the cell membrane.

whyNot.C: Every living cell, plant or animal, has a cell membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: What is the main function of red blood cells in humans?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which combines with oxygen in the lungs to form oxyhaemoglobin and releases it in the tissues.

whyNot.D: Blood clotting is the work of platelets.
whyNot.A: Antibodies are made by lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which vegetation zone of Nigeria has tall trees forming a closed canopy with several layers, high annual rainfall and high humidity all year?
questions.explanation: The tropical rainforest of southern Nigeria receives heavy rainfall for most of the year. Its tall evergreen trees form layered, closed canopies, with little light reaching the forest floor.

whyNot.D: Guinea savanna has tall grasses with scattered trees and a clear dry season, not a closed canopy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: In garden peas, tallness (T) is dominant over dwarfness (t). A heterozygous tall plant is crossed with a dwarf plant. What ratio of offspring is expected?
questions.explanation: The cross is Tt × tt. The tall parent gives T or t, the dwarf parent gives only t, so the offspring are Tt, Tt, tt, tt: two tall to two dwarf, which is 1 : 1.

whyNot.A: 3 : 1 comes from crossing two heterozygous plants (Tt × Tt).
whyNot.D: All tall would come from TT × tt.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: An arthropod has a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen and has three pairs of jointed legs. To which class does it belong?
questions.explanation: Insects such as the grasshopper and housefly have three body parts and three pairs of legs, usually with one or two pairs of wings and one pair of antennae.

whyNot.B: Arachnids such as spiders and scorpions have two body parts and four pairs of legs.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which sequence shows the levels of organisation in a multicellular organism, from the simplest to the most complex?
questions.explanation: Similar cells group together to form a tissue, different tissues form an organ, and organs working together form a system, such as the digestive system.

whyNot.A: An organ is made of several tissues, so tissue must come before organ.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: In which part of the human alimentary canal does the digestion of protein begin?
questions.explanation: Protein digestion begins in the stomach, where pepsin, working in acid conditions provided by hydrochloric acid, breaks proteins into polypeptides.

whyNot.D: Saliva has amylase for starch but no protein-digesting enzyme.
whyNot.C: Protein digestion is completed in the ileum, but it does not begin there.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which of the following is an adaptation of xerophytes, plants of very dry habitats?
options: Air spaces (aerenchyma) in the stem for floating
Many stomata on the upper leaf surface
questions.explanation: Sunken stomata trap a layer of moist air above them, which reduces water loss by transpiration. This helps plants survive in dry places like the Sahel.

whyNot.A: Large thin leaves lose a lot of water; they suit shady, moist habitats.
whyNot.C: Aerenchyma is an adaptation of hydrophytes such as water lettuce.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A normal human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a normal human sperm cell?
questions.explanation: Gametes are made by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number. A sperm therefore has 23 chromosomes, and fertilisation restores 46 in the zygote.

whyNot.A: 46 is the diploid number of body cells, not of gametes.
whyNot.D: 22 is the number of autosomes in a sperm; it also carries one sex chromosome, making 23.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: The pork tapeworm, Taenia solium, belongs to the phylum
questions.explanation: Tapeworms are flatworms (Platyhelminthes): their bodies are flat, ribbon-like and divided into proglottids, and they have no gut of their own.

whyNot.D: Nematodes such as Ascaris are roundworms with a round body and a complete gut.
whyNot.C: Annelids such as the earthworm are segmented worms with a body cavity.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A cell 0.25 mm long is viewed under a light microscope with an eyepiece lens of ×10 and an objective lens of ×40. How long will the image appear?
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective = 10 × 40 = ×400. Image length = actual length × magnification = 0.25 mm × 400 = 100 mm.

whyNot.A: 12.5 mm adds the lens powers (10 + 40 = 50) instead of multiplying them.
whyNot.D: 10 mm uses only the objective lens (0.25 × 40).

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which part of the human brain controls balance and the coordination of muscular movements?
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates muscle movements and keeps the body balanced, for example when walking or riding a bicycle.

whyNot.C: The cerebrum controls thinking, memory and voluntary actions.
whyNot.A: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as breathing and heartbeat.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: What is the main source of energy for almost all ecosystems?
questions.explanation: Green plants trap light energy from the sun during photosynthesis and store it in food. This energy then passes along food chains to consumers.

whyNot.B: Green plants pass energy on, but they get it from sunlight in the first place.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A person with genotype HbAS is best described as
options: A person with no sickle-cell allele at all
A person who can never pass the sickle-cell allele to a child
A sickle-cell anaemia patient who suffers frequent crises
A carrier of the sickle-cell allele who usually has no symptoms
questions.explanation: HbAS has one normal allele (A) and one sickle-cell allele (S). The normal allele is dominant, so the person is usually healthy, but can pass S on to half of their children on average.

whyNot.C: Sickle-cell anaemia occurs in people with genotype HbSS.
whyNot.B: Each child has a 1 in 2 chance of receiving the S allele from an HbAS parent.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which statement is true of mosses (bryophytes)?
options: The sporophyte is the main, independent plant
They have true roots, stems and leaves
They have no true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
questions.explanation: Mosses lack xylem and phloem, so they stay small and grow in damp places. They have rhizoids instead of true roots, reproduce by spores, and the gametophyte is the main plant.

whyNot.B: In mosses the sporophyte grows on, and depends on, the gametophyte; a dominant sporophyte is a feature of ferns and seed plants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which substances are produced when yeast respires anaerobically?
questions.explanation: Yeast breaks down glucose without oxygen to give ethanol and CO₂ (C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂). This is used in brewing and in making bread rise.

whyNot.B: Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in human muscle.
whyNot.C: Glucose and oxygen are the products of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: After fertilisation in a flowering plant, which part of the flower develops into the fruit?
questions.explanation: After fertilisation the ovary wall develops into the fruit wall (pericarp), while the ovules inside become the seeds.

whyNot.B: The ovule becomes the seed, not the fruit.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: In an ecological survey, a grass species was found in 12 out of 40 quadrats thrown at random in a field. What is the frequency of the species?
questions.explanation: Percentage frequency = (number of quadrats with the species ÷ total number of quadrats) × 100 = (12 ÷ 40) × 100 = 30%.

whyNot.A: 3.3% divides 40 by 12 the wrong way round; the number of quadrats with the species goes on top.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: In peas, round seed (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r) and yellow seed (Y) is dominant over green (y). If two plants of genotype RrYy are crossed, what fraction of the offspring is expected to have round, yellow seeds?
questions.explanation: Each parent makes four kinds of gametes (RY, Ry, rY, ry), giving 16 combinations. Those with at least one R and at least one Y are round and yellow: 9 out of 16, from the 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio.

whyNot.D: 3/16 is the fraction with round green or wrinkled yellow seeds.
whyNot.C: 3/4 is the fraction that are round (or that are yellow) when one trait is considered alone.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A vertebrate has moist skin without scales, lives partly in water and partly on land, and goes through metamorphosis from a tadpole. To which class does it belong?
questions.explanation: Toads and frogs are amphibians: their skin is moist and scaleless, they lay eggs in water, and the tadpole changes into the adult by metamorphosis.

whyNot.A: Reptiles such as the agama lizard have dry, scaly skin and lay shelled eggs on land.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: What is the function of ribosomes in a cell?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are tiny organelles, many attached to the endoplasmic reticulum, where amino acids are joined together to make proteins.

whyNot.A: Energy is released in the mitochondria.
whyNot.B: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: In humans, the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between the air and the blood takes place in the
questions.explanation: The alveoli are tiny air sacs with thin, moist walls and a rich supply of capillaries, so O₂ diffuses into the blood and CO₂ diffuses out.

whyNot.A: The trachea only carries air to and from the lungs; its walls are too thick for gaseous exchange.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead plants and animals and return minerals to the soil are called
questions.explanation: Decomposers feed on dead organic matter and break it down, releasing mineral salts back into the soil for plants to use. Without them, nutrients would not be recycled.

whyNot.C: Parasites feed on living hosts, not on dead matter.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. Which blood groups can their children have?
questions.explanation: The man (IᴬIᴮ) passes on Iᴬ or Iᴮ, and the woman (ii) can only pass on i. The children are Iᴬi (group A) or Iᴮi (group B). No child can be AB or O.

whyNot.D: A child would need Iᴬ and Iᴮ for AB, or two i alleles for O, but only one parent has each.
whyNot.A: The mother has no Iᴬ or Iᴮ allele to give, so AB is impossible.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which of the following animals is a reptile?
questions.explanation: The agama lizard has dry, scaly skin, breathes with lungs and lays shelled eggs on land, which are features of reptiles.

whyNot.D: The toad is an amphibian with moist, scaleless skin.
whyNot.B: The bat is a mammal: it has hair and feeds its young on milk.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which of these processes does NOT need energy from respiration?
questions.explanation: Diffusion is passive: molecules move from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration because of their own random movement. The other three need energy (ATP) from the cell.

whyNot.A: In phagocytosis the cell uses energy to change shape and engulf solid particles.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: What is the main function of xylem in a flowering plant?
options: Carrying water and mineral salts from the roots to the leaves
Carrying manufactured food from the leaves to other parts
Gaseous exchange between the plant and the air
questions.explanation: Xylem vessels are long, hollow tubes that carry water and dissolved mineral salts upwards from the roots. Their lignified walls also help support the plant.

whyNot.B: Carrying manufactured food (translocation) is the work of phloem.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A student counted 360 cassava plants in a rectangular farm plot measuring 30 m by 4 m. What is the population density of the cassava?
questions.explanation: Area = 30 m × 4 m = 120 m². Population density = number of plants ÷ area = 360 ÷ 120 = 3 plants per m².

whyNot.D: 12 divides by 30 only, ignoring the 4 m width.
whyNot.C: 90 divides by 4 only, ignoring the 30 m length.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: What is the basic unit of heredity that is passed from parents to offspring?
questions.explanation: A gene is a section of DNA on a chromosome that controls a particular characteristic. Genes are passed from parents to offspring in the gametes.

whyNot.A: Ribosomes make proteins using the instructions in genes, but they are not inherited as units of heredity.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Plasmodium, the organism that causes malaria, is placed in the kingdom
questions.explanation: Plasmodium is a single-celled organism with a true nucleus, so it is a protist (a protozoan). It is not a bacterium or a virus.

whyNot.A: Monera are bacteria, which have no true nucleus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A plant cell with 24 chromosomes (2n = 24) divides by meiosis. What is produced?
questions.explanation: Meiosis involves two divisions, so one cell gives four daughter cells. The chromosome number is halved, so each cell has 24 ÷ 2 = 12 chromosomes.

whyNot.C: Two cells with the same number as the parent is the result of mitosis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which endocrine gland is often called the master gland because its hormones control many other glands?
questions.explanation: The pituitary gland at the base of the brain releases hormones such as TSH and FSH that control the thyroid, adrenal glands and gonads, so it is called the master gland.

whyNot.C: The thyroid makes thyroxine, but its activity is itself controlled by the pituitary.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of mutualism?
options: A lion feeding on an antelope
Mistletoe (Loranthus) growing on a cocoa tree
A tapeworm living in the human intestine
An alga and a fungus living together as a lichen
questions.explanation: In a lichen, the alga makes food by photosynthesis for both partners, while the fungus gives shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Both benefit, so it is mutualism.

whyNot.C: The tapeworm benefits and the human is harmed, which is parasitism.
whyNot.B: Loranthus takes water and minerals from its host and harms it, so it is a (partial) parasite.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: A tall pea plant was crossed with a dwarf pea plant, and about half of the offspring were tall and half dwarf. Tallness (T) is dominant. What was the genotype of the tall parent?
options: It could be either TT or Tt
questions.explanation: The dwarf parent must be tt. Dwarf offspring (tt) need a t from each parent, so the tall parent must carry t as well as T: it is Tt. This is a test cross.

whyNot.B: A TT parent would give only T gametes, so all offspring would be tall (Tt).
whyNot.D: A tt plant is dwarf, not tall.
whyNot.C: A TT parent could not give any dwarf offspring, so the dwarf plants rule TT out.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which feature is shared by ALL arthropods?
options: A body divided into head, thorax and abdomen
Jointed legs and an exoskeleton containing chitin
questions.explanation: All arthropods, including insects, spiders, crabs and millipedes, have jointed appendages and a hard exoskeleton containing chitin, which they moult as they grow.

whyNot.B: Three pairs of legs is true of insects only; spiders have four pairs and millipedes have many.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: What is the main function of lysosomes in a cell?
options: Digesting worn-out organelles and engulfed materials with their enzymes
Controlling what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are small sacs containing digestive enzymes. They break down old organelles and materials taken into the cell, such as bacteria engulfed by white blood cells.

whyNot.D: Controlling what enters and leaves the cell is the job of the cell membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant, mainly through the stomata, is called
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from the leaf cells and its loss as vapour, mostly through the stomata. It helps pull water up the xylem.

whyNot.D: Guttation is the loss of liquid water droplets through special pores at the leaf edges, not water vapour.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which human activity contributes most to desertification in the northern parts of Nigeria?
options: Overgrazing and cutting down trees for firewood
questions.explanation: Overgrazing and felling trees remove the plant cover that holds the soil together. The bare soil dries out and is blown away by wind, so the land slowly turns into desert.

whyNot.A: Shelterbelts are planted to stop desertification by breaking the wind and holding the soil.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Albinism is controlled by a recessive allele. Two parents with normal skin colour have a child with albinism. What is the probability that their next child will have normal skin colour?
questions.explanation: An albino child (aa) means both parents must be carriers (Aa). The cross Aa × Aa gives AA, Aa, aA and aa, so 3 out of 4 children are expected to have normal skin. Each child has the same chance.

whyNot.B: 1/4 is the probability of another child with albinism.
whyNot.D: Having one albino child does not change the odds for the next child.

questions.subject: biology
questions.stem: Which of the following plants is a gymnosperm?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms such as pine bear naked seeds on cones and have no flowers or fruits. Maize and hibiscus are flowering plants (angiosperms).

whyNot.D: Ferns reproduce by spores and have no seeds, so they are pteridophytes, not gymnosperms.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Ada has ₦2,000. She can buy either an Economics textbook or a T-shirt, and she buys the textbook. What is the opportunity cost of her choice?
options: The T-shirt she did not buy
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next best alternative given up when a choice is made. Ada gave up the T-shirt to get the textbook, so the T-shirt is the opportunity cost.

whyNot.A: Opportunity cost is measured in the alternative forgone, not the money price paid.
whyNot.D: The textbook is what she chose, not what she sacrificed.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The basic economic problem facing every society arises because
options: governments do not plan the economy
money is not evenly shared among people
resources are scarce relative to human wants
questions.explanation: Human wants are unlimited while the resources for satisfying them are limited. This scarcity forces every society to choose what to produce, how and for whom.

whyNot.C: Unequal income is a problem, but scarcity would exist even if money were shared equally.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A point inside a country's production possibility curve shows that
options: the country has reached full employment
some resources are unemployed or used inefficiently
the country cannot produce that combination
questions.explanation: Points on the curve show full and efficient use of resources. A point inside the curve means the economy could produce more of both goods, so some resources are idle or wasted.

whyNot.D: Combinations outside the curve are unattainable; points inside are attainable.
whyNot.C: Improved technology shifts the whole curve outward; it is not shown by a point inside it.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: In a mixed economy, resources are allocated by
options: both the price mechanism and the government
questions.explanation: A mixed economy combines private enterprise guided by prices with government ownership and regulation. Nigeria is an example: private firms operate alongside government agencies and public enterprises.

whyNot.B: That describes a pure capitalist (market) economy.
whyNot.A: That describes a command or socialist economy.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: When the price of a loaf of bread rises from ₦50 to ₦60, the quantity demanded falls from 200 loaves to 150 loaves. What is the price elasticity of demand (ignoring the sign)?
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 50 ÷ 200 × 100 = 25%. Percentage change in price = 10 ÷ 50 × 100 = 20%. Elasticity = 25 ÷ 20 = 1.25, so demand is elastic.

whyNot.B: 0.8 divides the price change by the quantity change; it should be quantity change ÷ price change.
whyNot.C: 2.5 compares the 50-loaf fall with ₦20 instead of using percentage changes.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A large rise in the pump price of petrol is most likely to reduce the demand for
questions.explanation: Cars and petrol are complementary goods because they are used together. When petrol becomes dearer, running a car costs more, so the demand for cars falls.

whyNot.D: Bicycles are a substitute for motor transport, so their demand is more likely to rise.
whyNot.C: Bus rides can replace private car use, so their demand tends to rise rather than fall.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: If the government fixes the maximum price of rice below the equilibrium price, the most likely result is
options: a surplus of rice in the market
a shortage of rice and black marketing
a rise in the equilibrium price
an increase in the supply of rice
questions.explanation: At a price below equilibrium, quantity demanded is greater than quantity supplied, so there is a shortage. Buyers willing to pay more encourage black markets and hoarding.

whyNot.A: A surplus results from a minimum price set above equilibrium, not a maximum price below it.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The price of tea rises by 10% and, as a result, the quantity demanded of coffee rises by 15%. What is the cross elasticity of demand and what does it show?
questions.explanation: Cross elasticity = % change in quantity of coffee ÷ % change in price of tea = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5. A positive cross elasticity means the goods are substitutes.

whyNot.B: Complements have a negative cross elasticity: a rise in one price reduces demand for the other.
whyNot.A: 0.67 divides the price change by the quantity change, the wrong way round.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A cassava processor finds that 4 workers produce 60 bags of garri a week and 5 workers produce 72 bags. What is the marginal product of the fifth worker?
questions.explanation: Marginal product = change in total product ÷ change in labour = (72 − 60) ÷ (5 − 4) = 12 bags.

whyNot.A: 14.4 bags is the average product of 5 workers (72 ÷ 5).
whyNot.C: 15 bags is the average product of 4 workers (60 ÷ 4).

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following is a fixed cost for a bakery in the short run?
options: Wages of casual workers paid per loaf
questions.explanation: A fixed cost does not change with the level of output. Rent must be paid whether the bakery makes 10 loaves or 1,000, while flour, piece-rate wages and fuel rise with output.

whyNot.D: Flour is a variable cost: more bread needs more flour.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The law of diminishing returns states that as more units of a variable factor are added to a fixed factor,
questions.explanation: When extra workers are added to a fixed amount of land or machinery, each additional worker eventually adds less to output than the one before. Total product may still be rising while marginal product falls.

whyNot.D: Total product can keep rising for a while after marginal product begins to fall.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A firm's total cost schedule is: output 0 units, ₦120; 1 unit, ₦160; 2 units, ₦190; 3 units, ₦240. What is the average variable cost at 3 units of output?
questions.explanation: Fixed cost is the cost at zero output, ₦120. Variable cost at 3 units = 240 − 120 = ₦120, so AVC = 120 ÷ 3 = ₦40.

whyNot.A: ₦80 is average total cost (240 ÷ 3), which includes fixed cost.
whyNot.D: ₦50 is the marginal cost of the third unit (240 − 190).

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The function of money that removes the problem of double coincidence of wants is its use as a
questions.explanation: Under barter, a trader must find someone who has what he wants and wants what he has. Money as a medium of exchange lets him sell to anyone and buy from anyone.

whyNot.C: Store of value is about holding wealth over time, not about making exchange easier.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: If commercial banks keep a cash reserve ratio of 20%, how much in total deposits can the banking system create from a fresh cash deposit of ₦10,000?
questions.explanation: The money (credit) multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio = 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5. Total deposits = ₦10,000 × 5 = ₦50,000.

whyNot.D: ₦8,000 is only what the first bank can lend out after keeping 20% in reserve.
whyNot.C: ₦2,000 is the reserve the first bank must keep.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: When the Central Bank of Nigeria sells government securities to the public through open market operations, the effect is to
questions.explanation: Buyers pay for the securities with money drawn from their bank accounts, so cash flows out of the banking system into the CBN. Banks then have less to lend and the money supply falls.

whyNot.D: Buying securities from the public would increase the money supply; selling does the opposite.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Inflation described as "too much money chasing too few goods" is
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when total demand grows faster than the supply of goods and services, pulling prices up. Cost-push inflation comes from rising costs of production such as wages or fuel.

whyNot.A: Cost-push inflation starts from the supply side, through higher production costs.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A country's GDP is ₦500 billion. Its citizens earn ₦40 billion from abroad, while foreigners earn ₦70 billion in the country. What is its GNP?
questions.explanation: GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad. Net factor income = 40 − 70 = −₦30 billion, so GNP = 500 − 30 = ₦470 billion.

whyNot.C: ₦530 billion adds the net figure the wrong way; net factor income here is negative.
whyNot.A: ₦610 billion adds both flows instead of subtracting income paid to foreigners.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: In a given year, Nigeria's index of export prices is 120 and its index of import prices is 150. What are the terms of trade?
questions.explanation: Terms of trade = (index of export prices ÷ index of import prices) × 100 = (120 ÷ 150) × 100 = 80. A figure below 100 means the terms of trade are unfavourable.

whyNot.D: 125 puts import prices over export prices, the wrong way round.
whyNot.A: 30 is just the difference between the two indices.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The theory of comparative cost advantage in international trade is associated with
questions.explanation: David Ricardo developed the theory of comparative advantage, showing that countries gain by specialising in goods they produce at a lower opportunity cost. Adam Smith is linked with absolute advantage.

whyNot.C: Adam Smith explained absolute advantage and division of labour.
whyNot.A: Malthus is known for his theory of population.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: GDP at market prices is ₦800 billion, indirect taxes are ₦60 billion and subsidies are ₦20 billion. What is GDP at factor cost?
questions.explanation: GDP at factor cost = GDP at market prices − indirect taxes + subsidies = 800 − 60 + 20 = ₦760 billion. Taxes raise market prices above factor cost, while subsidies lower them.

whyNot.D: ₦840 billion adds taxes and subtracts subsidies, the reverse of the correct adjustment.
whyNot.B: ₦720 billion subtracts both taxes and subsidies.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Lionel Robbins defined economics as the science that studies human behaviour as a relationship between
options: ends and scarce means which have alternative uses
buyers and sellers in a market
questions.explanation: Robbins's scarcity definition stresses that wants (ends) are many while the means of satisfying them are scarce and can be put to different uses, so choices must be made.

whyNot.A: Studying the production and consumption of wealth is closer to the older wealth definition associated with Adam Smith.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The reward for the entrepreneur as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest and the entrepreneur, who organises the other factors and bears risk, earns profit.

whyNot.B: Rent is the reward for land.
whyNot.C: Interest is the reward for capital.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a capitalist economy?
options: Private ownership of the means of production
Prices fixed by the state for all goods
questions.explanation: In a capitalist (free market) economy, individuals and firms own land and capital and decide what to produce, guided by prices and the profit motive.

whyNot.A: Central planning is a feature of a socialist or command economy.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: An outward shift of a country's production possibility curve can be caused by
options: moving resources from one good to another
the discovery of new mineral resources
a fall in the population of working age
questions.explanation: An outward shift means the economy can produce more of both goods. More resources or better technology cause this; reallocating existing resources only moves the economy along the curve.

whyNot.D: Unemployment moves production to a point inside the curve; it does not shift the curve.
whyNot.A: Reallocating resources is a movement along the curve.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A fruit seller in Onitsha sells 40 baskets of oranges at ₦250 per basket. What is her total revenue?
questions.explanation: Total revenue = price × quantity sold = ₦250 × 40 = ₦10,000.

whyNot.A: ₦6.25 divides the price by the quantity instead of multiplying.
whyNot.D: ₦290 adds the price and quantity.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A bumper harvest of maize in the northern states will, other things being equal,
options: shift the supply curve of maize to the left
shift the demand curve for maize to the right
cause a movement up the supply curve
shift the supply curve of maize to the right
questions.explanation: A good harvest increases the quantity of maize offered at every price, so the whole supply curve shifts to the right and the price of maize tends to fall.

whyNot.A: A leftward shift is a fall in supply, as caused by drought or pests.
whyNot.C: A movement along the supply curve is caused by a change in the price of maize itself.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: If the demand for a commodity is price inelastic, an increase in its price will
options: reduce the quantity demanded to zero
questions.explanation: With inelastic demand, the percentage fall in quantity demanded is smaller than the percentage rise in price, so price × quantity rises.

whyNot.A: Total revenue falls after a price rise only when demand is elastic.
whyNot.D: Total revenue stays unchanged only when elasticity is exactly 1 (unitary).

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The demand and supply functions for a commodity are Qd = 100 − 2P and Qs = 20 + 2P. What are the equilibrium price and quantity?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium Qd = Qs: 100 − 2P = 20 + 2P, so 80 = 4P and P = ₦20. Then Q = 100 − 2(20) = 60 units.

whyNot.C: ₦40 comes from dividing 80 by 2 instead of 4.
whyNot.B: 40 units is 2P, not the quantity; substitute P into either function to get 60.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Five workers in a block-making yard produce 85 blocks in an hour. What is the average product of labour?
questions.explanation: Average product = total product ÷ number of workers = 85 ÷ 5 = 17 blocks per worker.

whyNot.A: 425 multiplies output by the number of workers instead of dividing.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A farm's total product as more workers are employed on a fixed piece of land is: 1 worker, 10 bags; 2 workers, 24 bags; 3 workers, 36 bags; 4 workers, 44 bags. Diminishing marginal returns set in when the farm employs
questions.explanation: Marginal products are 10, 14, 12 and 8 bags. Marginal product rises up to the second worker and first falls with the third worker (from 14 to 12 bags), so diminishing returns set in there.

whyNot.D: Total product is still rising at the fourth worker, but marginal product had already started falling with the third.
whyNot.A: The second worker's marginal product (14) is higher than the first's, so returns are still increasing.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The long run in production is a period in which
options: at least one factor is fixed
all factors of production can be varied
questions.explanation: In the short run at least one factor, such as factory size, is fixed. In the long run the firm has time to change all factors, including building new plants.

whyNot.B: Having at least one fixed factor defines the short run.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A large firm obtains discounts by buying its raw materials in bulk. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Internal economies of scale arise within a single firm as it grows, such as bulk-buying (marketing) economies. External economies benefit all firms in an industry, for example from good roads in an industrial area.

whyNot.D: External economies come from the growth of the industry or area, not from the firm's own size.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The quality of good money that allows it to be broken into smaller units for small purchases without losing value is
questions.explanation: Divisibility means money can be split into smaller denominations, such as naira and kobo, so that both large and small transactions can be made.

whyNot.D: Durability means money lasts a long time without wearing out.
whyNot.C: Portability means money is easy to carry.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following functions is performed by the Central Bank of Nigeria and not by commercial banks?
options: Accepting savings deposits from the public
Acting as lender of last resort to banks
questions.explanation: The CBN lends to commercial banks when they run short of cash, as lender of last resort. Accepting deposits and lending to the public are functions of commercial banks.

whyNot.A: Accepting savings deposits from the public is a core commercial bank function.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Using the quantity theory of money MV = PT, if the money supply is ₦2,000, the velocity of circulation is 5 and the volume of transactions is 500, what is the general price level?

whyNot.B: ₦4 leaves out the velocity of circulation (2,000 ÷ 500).
whyNot.C: ₦10,000 is MV, total spending, before dividing by the volume of transactions.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The main function of the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) is to
options: protect depositors by insuring their bank deposits
fix the exchange rate of the naira
collect taxes for the federal government
issue the naira notes and coins
questions.explanation: The NDIC insures deposits in licensed banks, so that depositors are paid up to an insured limit if a bank fails. It also helps supervise banks.

whyNot.D: Issuing the currency is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: In Country X one worker can produce 10 metres of cloth or 5 bags of wheat; in Country Y one worker can produce 6 metres of cloth or 4 bags of wheat. Which statement is correct?
options: Y has a comparative advantage in cloth
Y has a comparative advantage in wheat
X has a comparative advantage in wheat
questions.explanation: In X, 1 bag of wheat costs 10 ÷ 5 = 2 metres of cloth; in Y it costs 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 metres. Y gives up less cloth per bag of wheat, so Y has the comparative advantage in wheat and X in cloth.

whyNot.D: X has an absolute advantage in both goods, but its opportunity cost of wheat (2 metres of cloth) is higher than Y's.
whyNot.A: Trade is beneficial because the opportunity costs differ between the two countries.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following is an invisible item in Nigeria's balance of payments?
options: Insurance services bought from a foreign company
questions.explanation: Invisible items are trade in services such as insurance, shipping, banking and tourism. Physical goods like crude oil, cars and cocoa are visible items.

whyNot.B: Crude oil is a physical good, so it is a visible export.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A country has a national income of ₦900 billion and a population of 45 million. What is its per capita income?
questions.explanation: Per capita income = national income ÷ population = ₦900,000,000,000 ÷ 45,000,000 = ₦20,000.

whyNot.C: ₦2,000 comes from losing a zero when converting billions and millions.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established in
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was established by the Treaty of Lagos in May 1975 to promote economic integration and trade among West African countries.

whyNot.C: 1963 is when the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was formed.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following is a free good?
questions.explanation: A free good is available in quantities large enough to satisfy all wants, so it has no price and no opportunity cost. Air is the usual example; bottled water and electricity need scarce resources to produce.

whyNot.D: Water is processed and packaged using scarce resources, so it is an economic good.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A farmer can grow either 100 tubers of yam or 50 baskets of cassava on her land, or any combination along a straight-line production possibility curve. What is the opportunity cost of one basket of cassava?
questions.explanation: Giving up all 100 yams yields 50 baskets of cassava, so 1 basket of cassava costs 100 ÷ 50 = 2 tubers of yam.

whyNot.A: 0.5 is the opportunity cost of one yam in baskets of cassava, not the other way round.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: An economic system in which a central planning authority decides what, how and for whom to produce is a
questions.explanation: In a socialist (command) economy, the state owns most resources and a central planning authority makes the major production decisions instead of the price mechanism.

whyNot.A: In a capitalist economy these decisions are made by private individuals through the price mechanism.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following is a normative statement?
options: Nigeria became a member of OPEC in 1971
A rise in price reduces the quantity demanded
The government should reduce the price of petrol
questions.explanation: A normative statement expresses an opinion about what ought to be and cannot be tested by facts. Positive statements, like the other three, describe what is and can be checked.

whyNot.A: Nigeria's OPEC membership date is a fact that can be verified, so it is positive.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The law of demand states that, other things being equal,
options: the higher the price, the lower the quantity demanded
a rise in income increases the price of goods
the higher the price, the higher the quantity demanded
questions.explanation: The law of demand describes an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded, holding income, tastes and other prices constant. This gives the demand curve its downward slope.

whyNot.D: A positive relationship between price and quantity describes the law of supply.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Which of the following goods is an exception to the law of demand?
options: Exercise books bought by a student
Expensive jewellery bought to show off wealth
questions.explanation: Goods of ostentation (Veblen goods) are bought partly because they are expensive, so some buyers demand more at higher prices. This produces an abnormal, upward-sloping demand curve.

whyNot.A: Exercise books are an ordinary good: a student buys fewer when the price rises.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: When the price of a pair of sandals rises from ₦100 to ₦120, the quantity supplied rises from 400 to 440 pairs. What is the price elasticity of supply?
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity supplied = 40 ÷ 400 × 100 = 10%. Percentage change in price = 20 ÷ 100 × 100 = 20%. Elasticity of supply = 10 ÷ 20 = 0.5, so supply is inelastic.

whyNot.C: 2 divides the price change by the quantity change, the wrong way round.
whyNot.B: 0.1 is the proportionate change in quantity alone, not divided by the change in price.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: When the government places a tax on a commodity whose demand is perfectly inelastic, the burden of the tax falls
questions.explanation: With perfectly inelastic demand, buyers purchase the same quantity whatever the price, so sellers can raise the price by the full amount of the tax. Consumers therefore bear the whole burden.

whyNot.D: Producers bear the whole tax when demand is perfectly elastic, since any price rise loses all their customers.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A firm's total cost is ₦500 when it produces 10 units and ₦560 when it produces 12 units. What is the marginal cost per unit over this range?
questions.explanation: Marginal cost = change in total cost ÷ change in output = (560 − 500) ÷ (12 − 10) = 60 ÷ 2 = ₦30 per unit.

whyNot.D: ₦60 is the change in total cost, not yet divided by the 2 extra units.
whyNot.B: ₦46.67 is the average cost at 12 units (560 ÷ 12).

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A firm maximises its profit at the output where
options: total revenue is at its highest
average cost is at its lowest
average revenue equals average fixed cost
questions.explanation: If marginal revenue is above marginal cost, producing one more unit adds to profit; if it is below, the unit reduces profit. Profit is therefore greatest where MC = MR.

whyNot.A: Maximising total revenue ignores costs, so it does not maximise profit.
whyNot.C: The lowest average cost is the most efficient output, but not necessarily the most profitable one.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: Cement factories are often sited near limestone deposits mainly because of
questions.explanation: Limestone is bulky and loses much weight during processing, so it is cheaper to make cement near the deposits than to transport the raw material far away.

whyNot.A: Market-oriented industries are those whose products gain weight or are perishable, such as bakeries.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A firm's total fixed cost is ₦600. At an output of 40 units, its average variable cost is ₦15. What is its average total cost at this output?
questions.explanation: Average fixed cost = 600 ÷ 40 = ₦15. Average total cost = AFC + AVC = 15 + 15 = ₦30.

whyNot.D: ₦15 is only the average variable cost (or only AFC); ATC adds the two.
whyNot.C: ₦615 adds total fixed cost to average variable cost, mixing totals and averages.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A man who owns a goat wants to exchange it for only a small quantity of salt. The problem of barter he faces is
options: lack of a store of value
questions.explanation: A goat cannot be cut into small parts without destroying its value, so it is hard to exchange for a small quantity of another good. Money solves this because it is divisible.

whyNot.C: Under barter there is no money in circulation at all.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: The cash reserve ratio is 10%. A customer makes a fresh cash deposit of ₦5,000 into the banking system. How much new credit (loans) can the banking system create from it?
questions.explanation: Total deposits = ₦5,000 ÷ 0.1 = ₦50,000. The original ₦5,000 was a cash deposit, so the new credit created = 50,000 − 5,000 = ₦45,000.

whyNot.B: ₦50,000 is total deposits, which includes the original ₦5,000 cash.
whyNot.A: ₦4,500 is only the first loan made by the first bank.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: If the Central Bank of Nigeria raises its monetary policy (bank) rate, the most likely effect is that
options: commercial banks lend more to customers
the cash reserve ratio falls automatically
commercial banks raise their lending rates and borrowing falls
questions.explanation: A higher central bank rate makes it dearer for banks to borrow, so they charge customers more. Borrowing and spending fall, which reduces the money supply and helps control inflation.

whyNot.C: A higher rate is a tight monetary policy that reduces, not increases, the money supply.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: During a period of high inflation, which group is likely to gain?
questions.explanation: Inflation reduces the real value of money. Debtors repay loans with money worth less than when they borrowed, so they gain while creditors lose.

whyNot.D: Creditors lose because the money repaid buys less than the money lent.
whyNot.C: Fixed incomes buy less as prices rise.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A country's GNP is ₦650 billion and depreciation (capital consumption) is ₦50 billion. What is its net national product?
questions.explanation: NNP = GNP − depreciation = 650 − 50 = ₦600 billion.

whyNot.D: ₦700 billion adds depreciation instead of subtracting it.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A major problem in measuring national income in Nigeria is
options: the existence of a central bank
the large amount of subsistence production that is not marketed
the use of the naira as currency
questions.explanation: Many farmers consume what they produce, and much activity is not recorded, so it is hard to value. Poor records and illiteracy add to the difficulty of measuring national income.

whyNot.D: Nigeria does export goods, notably crude oil, so this is false.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: A government that places tariffs on imported textiles to protect a new local textile industry is applying the
questions.explanation: The infant industry argument holds that new local industries need temporary protection from established foreign competitors until they grow large and efficient enough to compete.

whyNot.C: Free trade means removing tariffs, not imposing them.

questions.subject: economics
questions.stem: In a year, a country's visible exports are ₦1,200 billion, its visible imports are ₦1,450 billion and its net invisible earnings are +₦100 billion. What is the balance on its current account?
questions.explanation: Balance of trade = 1,200 − 1,450 = −₦250 billion. Adding net invisibles: −250 + 100 = −₦150 billion, a current account deficit.

whyNot.C: −₦250 billion is the balance of trade (visibles only); the current account also includes invisibles.
whyNot.A: −₦350 billion subtracts the invisible earnings instead of adding them.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The supreme legal power of a state to make and enforce laws within its territory without external control is known as
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the supreme, final legal authority of the state over everyone within its territory. Jean Bodin and John Austin are the classical writers on the idea.

whyNot.C: Legitimacy is the acceptance by the people of a government's right to rule, not the supreme legal power itself.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which of the following countries is usually cited as having an unwritten constitution?
questions.explanation: The British constitution is not contained in a single document; it is found in statutes, judicial decisions, conventions and works of authority. The USA, Nigeria and Ghana all have written constitutions.

whyNot.B: The USA has the oldest written national constitution still in use (1787).

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The deliberate drawing of constituency boundaries to give one political party an unfair advantage is called
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering is the manipulation of constituency boundaries for partisan advantage. Ordinary delimitation is the neutral, lawful division of a country into constituencies.

whyNot.D: Delimitation is the normal process of fixing constituency boundaries; it becomes gerrymandering only when it is manipulated for advantage.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: How many members make up the Senate of Nigeria under the 1999 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Each of the 36 states elects three senators and the FCT elects one, giving 109 senators. The House of Representatives has 360 members.

whyNot.A: 360 is the membership of the House of Representatives.
whyNot.D: 469 is the total membership of both chambers together (109 + 360).

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established by a treaty signed in
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Treaty was signed in Lagos on 28 May 1975. Its headquarters is now in Abuja.

whyNot.B: Abuja is the present headquarters of ECOWAS, but the treaty was signed in Lagos.
whyNot.A: Addis Ababa in 1963 is where the OAU was founded.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The concept of the rule of law is most closely associated with
questions.explanation: A. V. Dicey explained the rule of law in his 1885 work on the law of the constitution, stressing the supremacy of law, equality before the law and the protection of rights by the courts.

whyNot.D: Montesquieu is associated with the separation of powers.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The doctrine of separation of powers was popularised by Montesquieu in his book
questions.explanation: Montesquieu published The Spirit of the Laws in 1748, arguing that liberty is best protected when legislative, executive and judicial powers are held by separate organs.

whyNot.C: The Social Contract was written by Jean-Jacques Rousseau.
whyNot.A: Leviathan was written by Thomas Hobbes.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: In a parliamentary system of government, ministers are collectively responsible to
questions.explanation: Under collective responsibility, the cabinet stands or falls together before parliament; if it loses a vote of no confidence, it must resign or seek a fresh election.

whyNot.C: The head of state in a parliamentary system is largely ceremonial; the cabinet answers to parliament.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which of the following is a judicial control over delegated legislation?
options: Laying the regulation before the legislature
Passing a vote of no confidence
questions.explanation: The courts control delegated legislation by declaring a rule ultra vires (beyond the powers granted by the parent law) and therefore void. Laying rules before the legislature is a legislative, not judicial, control.

whyNot.B: Laying before the legislature is a parliamentary (legislative) control.
whyNot.D: Assent relates to bills passed by the legislature, and it is an executive act, not a judicial one.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A constitution is described as rigid when
options: it cannot be interpreted by the courts
its amendment requires a special procedure different from that for ordinary laws
it was drafted by a military government
it is contained in several documents
questions.explanation: A rigid constitution can only be amended by a special, more difficult procedure, such as a two-thirds majority in the legislature plus approval by the component states. Nigeria's 1999 Constitution (section 9) is rigid.

whyNot.D: Being contained in several documents describes an unwritten constitution, not rigidity.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: An electoral system in which parties win seats in proportion to the share of votes they receive is
questions.explanation: Under proportional representation, a party that wins, for example, 30 per cent of the votes gets roughly 30 per cent of the seats, often through party lists.

whyNot.A: In the simple majority (first-past-the-post) system the candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins the seat outright.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The main difference between a political party and a pressure group is that a political party
options: has members drawn from all over the country
seeks to win elections and control the government
questions.explanation: Both parties and pressure groups try to influence policy, but only a political party sponsors candidates for elections with the aim of forming the government.

whyNot.B: Influencing policy is common to both; it is the main aim of a pressure group.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: After the 1959 federal elections in Nigeria, the federal government was formed by a coalition of
questions.explanation: No party won an overall majority in 1959, so the Northern People's Congress (NPC) formed a coalition with the NCNC. Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa of the NPC became Prime Minister, and the Action Group (AG) formed the opposition.

whyNot.B: The Action Group, led by Obafemi Awolowo, was the official opposition after 1959.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Regionalism was introduced into Nigeria's constitutional development by the
questions.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 divided Nigeria into three regions (Northern, Western and Eastern), each with a regional House of Assembly.

whyNot.A: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 introduced federalism, building on the regions created in 1946.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which section of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria (as amended) declares the supremacy of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Section 1(1) states that the Constitution is supreme and binding on all authorities and persons, and section 1(3) makes any law inconsistent with it void to the extent of the inconsistency.

whyNot.A: Section 4 vests legislative powers in the National Assembly and the state Houses of Assembly.
whyNot.D: Section 33 protects the right to life.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution are
options: enforceable only in the Supreme Court
non-justiciable, so they cannot be enforced in a court of law
the same as the fundamental human rights
questions.explanation: Section 6(6)(c) of the 1999 Constitution provides that the courts' judicial powers do not extend to questions about whether the government has complied with Chapter II. They are guidelines for government, not enforceable rights.

whyNot.C: Fundamental human rights are in Chapter IV and are justiciable (enforceable in court).

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which of the following is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council?
questions.explanation: The five permanent members, each with the veto, are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States. Germany, Japan and Nigeria can only serve as elected non-permanent members.

whyNot.B: Nigeria has served several terms as an elected non-permanent member, but it is not a permanent member.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was replaced by the African Union (AU) in
questions.explanation: The OAU, founded in Addis Ababa on 25 May 1963, was replaced by the African Union, which was launched in Durban, South Africa, in July 2002.

whyNot.D: 1963 is the year the OAU was founded.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: In 1961 Nigeria broke off diplomatic relations with France mainly because France
options: blocked Nigeria's admission to the United Nations
carried out atomic bomb tests in the Sahara
questions.explanation: The Balewa government severed diplomatic ties with France in January 1961 in protest against French atomic tests in the Sahara Desert, which it considered a danger to Africa.

whyNot.C: French sympathy for Biafra came during the civil war (1967–70), years after the 1961 break.
whyNot.B: Nigeria was admitted to the UN on 7 October 1960 without obstruction.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A government in which political power is controlled by the wealthy few is called
questions.explanation: Plutocracy is rule by the rich. Gerontocracy is rule by elders, theocracy is rule by religious leaders and aristocracy is rule by a noble or 'best' few.

whyNot.C: Aristocracy is rule by a privileged noble class, defined by birth or merit, not simply by wealth.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Democracy was defined as 'government of the people, by the people and for the people' by
questions.explanation: US President Abraham Lincoln used these words in his Gettysburg Address of 1863, and they are the most quoted definition of democracy.

whyNot.A: Aristotle classified governments but did not give this definition.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A federal system of government is one in which
options: the head of state is a hereditary monarch
all powers are concentrated in the central government
powers are shared by the constitution between a central government and component units
component units are sovereign and may leave the union at will
questions.explanation: In a federation the constitution divides powers between the central government and the states or regions, each being supreme in its own sphere. Nigeria, the USA and India are examples.

whyNot.B: Concentration of power at the centre describes a unitary system.
whyNot.D: Sovereign units that can withdraw describe a confederation.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The right of citizens to vote in elections is known as
questions.explanation: Franchise (or suffrage) is the right to vote. Universal adult suffrage means every adult citizen, subject to minor legal limits, may vote.

whyNot.A: A mandate is the authority given to a winning party or candidate by the voters.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria were amalgamated in 1914 by
questions.explanation: Sir Frederick (later Lord) Lugard amalgamated the two protectorates on 1 January 1914 and became the first Governor-General of Nigeria.

whyNot.A: Sir Hugh Clifford gave his name to the 1922 Constitution.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York, USA. Geneva hosts a major UN office, and The Hague is the seat of the International Court of Justice.

whyNot.A: The Hague is the seat of the International Court of Justice, not the UN headquarters.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: When the citizens of a state accept that their government has the right to rule, the government is said to have
questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the people's acceptance of a government's right to exercise authority over them. It comes from things like free elections and respect for the constitution.

whyNot.C: Sovereignty is the supreme legal power of the state, which exists whether or not a particular government is popular.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The process by which individuals acquire political values, beliefs and attitudes is called
questions.explanation: Political socialisation is the learning process through agents such as the family, school, peer groups, religious bodies and the mass media.

whyNot.A: Political culture is the set of values and attitudes itself; socialisation is how people acquire it.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: In a presidential system of government, the president is
options: head of state only, while a prime minister heads the government
both head of state and head of government
questions.explanation: In a presidential system such as Nigeria's since 1979 (and the USA's), the executive president combines the roles of head of state and head of government.

whyNot.A: A separate prime minister as head of government is a feature of the parliamentary system.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which of the following best helps to secure the independence of the judiciary?
options: Payment of judges' salaries at the discretion of the executive
Election of judges by the legislature every year
Appointment of judges by the ruling party
questions.explanation: When judges cannot easily be removed except for misconduct or incapacity, through a laid-down procedure, they can decide cases without fear. Fixed salaries charged on the Consolidated Revenue Fund also help.

whyNot.A: Salaries at the executive's discretion would make judges dependent on the executive.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A feature of a confederation is that
options: the central government is stronger than the component units
the component units retain their sovereignty
there is only one level of government
the component units cannot withdraw from the union
questions.explanation: In a confederation, independent states join for limited purposes but keep their sovereignty and can withdraw. The central authority is weak and depends on the member states.

whyNot.A: A strong centre is typical of a federation or unitary state, not a confederation.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The electoral system in which the candidate with the highest number of votes wins, even without an absolute majority, is the
questions.explanation: Under the simple majority or first-past-the-post system, the candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins, even if he or she has less than half the votes.

whyNot.D: A second ballot (run-off) is used precisely when no candidate gets an absolute majority in the first round.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The removal of an elected representative by the voters of the constituency before the end of the term is known as
questions.explanation: Recall allows constituents to remove their representative before the term ends. Section 69 of the 1999 Constitution provides for the recall of members of the National Assembly.

whyNot.C: Impeachment is removal by the legislature (for example of a President or Governor), not by the voters.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution, elections into local government councils in a state are conducted by the
questions.explanation: Section 197 and the Third Schedule (Part II) of the 1999 Constitution establish a State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) in each state to conduct local government elections.

whyNot.B: INEC conducts federal and state elections, such as presidential, governorship and legislative elections, but not local government council elections in the states.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The elective principle was first introduced into Nigeria by the
questions.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 allowed four elected members in the Legislative Council: three from Lagos and one from Calabar. This encouraged the formation of the Nigerian National Democratic Party in 1923.

whyNot.B: The Richards Constitution of 1946 is known for introducing regionalism.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Under the 1963 Republican Constitution of Nigeria, the President was
options: both head of state and head of government
the leader of the majority party in parliament
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on 1 October 1963 but kept the parliamentary system. The President (Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe) was a ceremonial head of state, while executive power lay with the Prime Minister.

whyNot.B: An executive president combining both roles came with the 1979 Constitution.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The 'federal character' principle is provided for in which section of the 1999 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Section 14(3) requires that the composition of the Government of the Federation and its agencies reflect the federal character of Nigeria, so that no few states or ethnic or other sectional groups dominate. The Federal Character Commission enforces it.

whyNot.B: Section 6(6)(c) makes Chapter II non-justiciable.
whyNot.C: Section 153 lists the federal executive bodies such as INEC.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth in 1995 mainly because of
options: its refusal to pay Commonwealth subscriptions
a border war with a member state
the execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and other Ogoni activists under military rule
questions.explanation: After the military government executed Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists in November 1995, the Commonwealth suspended Nigeria. It was restored to full membership after the return to civilian rule in 1999.

whyNot.B: Nigeria has never left ECOWAS; it is a founding member.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The ECOWAS Ceasefire Monitoring Group (ECOMOG) was first deployed in 1990 to
questions.explanation: ECOMOG, in which Nigeria played the leading role, was first deployed to Liberia in August 1990 to help end the civil war there. It later intervened in Sierra Leone in the late 1990s.

whyNot.C: ECOMOG went into Sierra Leone later, in the late 1990s.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Since independence, the centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy has been
questions.explanation: Nigerian governments have consistently made Africa the centrepiece of foreign policy, for example by supporting decolonisation, opposing apartheid and leading in ECOWAS and the OAU/AU.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Authority differs from power mainly because authority is
options: the ability to compel obedience by force
always backed by the armed forces
power that is recognised as legitimate
questions.explanation: Power is the ability to make others act as one wishes, even by force. Authority is power that people accept as rightful, for example because it comes from the constitution or tradition.

whyNot.A: The ability to compel by force describes power (or coercion), not authority.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A system of government in which rulers govern in the name of God or according to religious law is
questions.explanation: In a theocracy, religious leaders rule, or rulers claim to govern according to divine law. Some states have made religious law the basis of their constitution.

whyNot.A: A monarchy is headed by a king or queen; it is not necessarily religious.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A constitution that can be amended by the same procedure used for passing ordinary laws is said to be
questions.explanation: A flexible constitution can be changed by a simple majority of the legislature, like any ordinary law. The British constitution is the usual example.

whyNot.C: A rigid constitution needs a special amendment procedure.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which of the following countries is a classic example of a two-party system?
questions.explanation: In the USA, the Democratic and Republican parties have long dominated elections, making it the standard example of a two-party system.

whyNot.A: China is governed by a single ruling party.
whyNot.C: India has many national and regional parties, a multi-party system.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: How many local government areas (including the area councils of the FCT) are listed in the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The First Schedule lists 768 local government areas in the 36 states plus 6 area councils in the Federal Capital Territory, a total of 774.

whyNot.B: 768 is the number in the states alone, without the 6 FCT area councils.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was founded on 25 May 1963 in
questions.explanation: African leaders signed the OAU Charter in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on 25 May 1963. Addis Ababa remains the headquarters of its successor, the African Union.

whyNot.B: Durban, South Africa, is where the African Union was launched in 2002.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The power of the President to veto a bill passed by the legislature is an example of
questions.explanation: Checks and balances allow each organ of government to limit the others. The executive's veto checks the legislature, which in turn can override the veto (section 58(5) of the 1999 Constitution).

whyNot.A: Judicial review is the courts' power to declare laws or actions unconstitutional, a check by the judiciary.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A state differs from a nation mainly because a state
options: has a government exercising sovereignty over a defined territory
always consists of a single ethnic group
is bound together by a common history and culture
is made up of people who share a common language
questions.explanation: A state is a political and legal entity with population, defined territory, government and sovereignty. A nation is a group of people bound by common identity such as language, culture or history, and may not have a state of its own.

whyNot.C: Common history and culture are features of a nation, not what defines a state.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: A vote of no confidence is a feature of the
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive depends on the support of parliament; if parliament passes a vote of no confidence, the prime minister and cabinet must resign or call an election.

whyNot.B: In a presidential system the president has a fixed term and is removed only by impeachment, not by a vote of no confidence.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: An official appointed to investigate complaints by citizens against maladministration by public officials is called
questions.explanation: The ombudsman investigates citizens' complaints against public officials. In Nigeria this role is performed by the Public Complaints Commission, established in 1975.

whyNot.C: The Auditor-General audits public accounts; he or she does not handle individual citizens' complaints.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The principle that civil servants should not be publicly praised or blamed for the policies they help to make is known as
questions.explanation: Under anonymity, civil servants remain in the background while ministers take public credit or blame for government policies.

whyNot.D: Permanence means civil servants keep their jobs when governments change.
whyNot.A: Neutrality means civil servants serve any government in power without party bias.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: An election held to fill a seat that becomes vacant through the death or resignation of a member is a
questions.explanation: A by-election fills a single vacancy that arises between general elections, for example when a legislator dies or resigns.

whyNot.C: A primary election is held within a party to choose its candidates.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)?
questions.explanation: The Third Schedule of the 1999 Constitution gives INEC powers to organise federal and state elections, register political parties, monitor their finances and register voters.

whyNot.D: Interpreting the Constitution is the work of the courts.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), formed in 1944, was led at its founding by
options: Ahmadu Bello and Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
questions.explanation: The NCNC was formed in August 1944 with Herbert Macaulay as its first president and Nnamdi Azikiwe as general secretary; Azikiwe became its leader after Macaulay died in 1946.

whyNot.B: Awolowo and Akintola were leaders of the Action Group (AG).
whyNot.A: Ahmadu Bello and Tafawa Balewa were leaders of the Northern People's Congress (NPC).

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Federalism was formally introduced into Nigeria by the
questions.explanation: The Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 made Nigeria a federation of three regions and the federal territory of Lagos, dividing powers between the federal and regional governments.

whyNot.A: The Richards Constitution of 1946 introduced regionalism, which prepared the ground for federalism.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Nigeria's four regions were replaced by twelve states on 27 May 1967 by the government of
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon created twelve states by decree on 27 May 1967, shortly before the civil war (1967–70). General Murtala Mohammed later increased the number to 19 in 1976.

whyNot.D: Murtala Mohammed's government created 19 states in 1976.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Under section 143 of the 1999 Constitution, the President is removed from office through impeachment when the report of the investigating panel is adopted by
options: not less than two-thirds of all the members of each House of the National Assembly
a simple majority of the Senate only
questions.explanation: Section 143 requires a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds majority of all the members of each House to adopt the panel's report, after which the President stands removed from office.

whyNot.D: Section 143(10) excludes the courts from impeachment proceedings.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: Nigeria became a member of the United Nations in
questions.explanation: Nigeria was admitted to the UN on 7 October 1960, a week after independence on 1 October 1960, as its 99th member.

whyNot.C: 1945 is when the UN itself was founded.
whyNot.A: 1963 is the year Nigeria became a republic and the OAU was founded.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The principal judicial organ of the United Nations is the
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice, which sits at The Hague in the Netherlands, settles legal disputes between states and gives advisory opinions.

whyNot.D: The Security Council is responsible for maintaining international peace and security, not for judging cases.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: The diplomatic representative of one Commonwealth country in another Commonwealth country is known as a
questions.explanation: Commonwealth members exchange High Commissioners rather than ambassadors. A Nigerian envoy in Ghana or the UK is therefore a High Commissioner.

whyNot.B: The Secretary-General heads the Commonwealth Secretariat in London; he or she is not a country's envoy.

questions.subject: government
questions.stem: In Aristotle's classification of governments, the corrupt form of aristocracy is
questions.explanation: Aristotle saw oligarchy as the perversion of aristocracy, where the few rule for their own interest. Tyranny is the corrupt form of monarchy and democracy (mob rule) the corrupt form of polity.

whyNot.D: Tyranny is the corrupt form of monarchy (rule by one).
